# Parentage of Patrick Flynn (b. ~1845, d. 1908, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania)

## Research Question

Who were the parents of Patrick Flynn, born approximately 1845 in Ireland, who died 12 March 1908 in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania?

## Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that **Thomas Flynn** was the father of Patrick Flynn. No evidence of Patrick's mother has been recovered to date. This conclusion is graded **probable**: research is not yet exhaustive (a search of Schuylkill County probate records for Thomas Flynn's estate is still in progress), and the strongest direct evidence carries a secondary informant. The conclusion may be revisited and strengthened as additional records are searched.

## Evidence

### 1. 1908 Death Certificate (original; direct evidence; secondary information)

Patrick Flynn's 1908 Pennsylvania death certificate explicitly names Thomas Flynn as Patrick's father.¹ This is an original record. For the parentage fact, it constitutes direct evidence — the record states the relationship in so many words. The informant was James Brown (son-in-law), who was not personally present at Patrick's birth and had no firsthand knowledge of Patrick's parentage; his information is therefore secondary. Secondary informants are more susceptible to error on parentage facts, especially when the reported father had likely been deceased for decades by 1908. Nonetheless, this is the only record in this study that explicitly names Patrick's father, and it is consistent with all other evidence gathered.

### 2. 1850 Federal Census — co-enumeration in Thomas Flynn's household (original; indirect evidence; indeterminate information)

The 1850 U.S. Federal Census for Schuylkill County enumerated Patrick Flynn, age 5, born Ireland, in dwelling 84, the household of Thomas Flynn (head, age approximately 32, born Ireland).² Patrick was the only individual of that name and approximate age found in Schuylkill County in that enumeration. This source is an original record. The 1850 census does not state household relationships explicitly — that column was not introduced until 1880. Patrick's position as a child in Thomas's household is inferred from his age, shared surname, and placement in the household listing, making this assertion indirect evidence of parentage. The informant for household members' names, ages, and birthplaces is unidentified (most likely a household member, possibly a neighbor); information quality is therefore indeterminate. The Ancestry.com derivative index of the same census confirms the same household and shows no transcription discrepancy.

### 3. 1860 Federal Census — continued co-enumeration ten years later (original; indirect evidence; indeterminate information)

Ten years later, the 1860 U.S. Federal Census again enumerated Patrick Flynn, age 15, born Ireland, in the household of Thomas Flynn (head), dwelling 112, family 119, in Schuylkill County.³ The derived birth year (approximately 1845), birthplace (Ireland), county of residence, and head of household all match the 1850 record exactly. This decade-long continuity of co-enumeration in Thomas's household substantially corroborates a parent-child relationship. As with the 1850 census, the 1860 census does not explicitly state relationships; the parentage inference is indirect, derived from household position and shared surname. This is an independent original record from the same county.

## Conflict: Birthplace Discrepancy (Resolved)

The 1850 and 1860 censuses record Patrick's birthplace as Ireland; the 1908 death certificate records it as Pennsylvania (c_001, resolved). The two contemporaneous census records — whose informants likely had firsthand knowledge of Patrick's birthplace, recorded within a few years of the event — outweigh the death certificate's secondary informant reporting 63 years after the fact. The son-in-law informant may have confused Patrick's place of childhood residence (Pennsylvania) with his place of birth, or may simply not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child. Ireland is accepted as Patrick's birthplace; the Pennsylvania entry on the death certificate is attributed to informant error.

## Research Scope and Limitations

Searches were conducted in the 1850 and 1860 U.S. Federal Censuses for Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, via FamilySearch (original images), Ancestry.com (independent derivative index), and MyHeritage (no relevant results — this collection appears not to be indexed there). Patrick Flynn's 1908 death certificate was found on FamilySearch. A search of Schuylkill County probate records for Thomas Flynn's estate (expected ca. 1870–1890) is in progress and not yet complete; a will or estate administration naming Patrick as a son would meaningfully strengthen this conclusion. Marriage records for Patrick Flynn, the 1870 and 1880 census enumerations, church baptismal records, and Catholic parish registers for the Flynn family have not yet been searched — these record types could independently corroborate or refine this finding. Research is not yet declared exhaustive.

---

² 1850 U.S. Census, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, population schedule, dwelling 84, family 91, Thomas Flynn household; NARA microfilm publication M432, roll 810; digital image, FamilySearch.org, accessed 1 May 2026.

³ 1860 U.S. Census, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, population schedule, dwelling 112, family 119, Thomas Flynn household; NARA microfilm publication M653, roll 1141; digital image, FamilySearch.org, accessed 2 May 2026.

The 1850 and 1860 censuses record Patrick's birthplace as Ireland; the 1908 death certificate records it as Pennsylvania (c_001, resolved). The two contemporaneous census records — whose informants likely had firsthand knowledge of Patrick's birthplace, recorded within a few years of the event — outweigh the death certificate's secondary informant reporting 63 years after the fact. The son-in-law informant may have confused Patrick's place of childhood residence (Pennsylvania) with his place of birth, or may simply not have known Patrick was born in Ireland before immigrating as a young child. Ireland is accepted as Patrick's birthplace; the Pennsylvania entry on the death certificate is attributed to informant error.

## Research Scope and Limitations

Searches were conducted in the 1850 and 1860 U.S. Federal Censuses for Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, via FamilySearch (original images), Ancestry.com (independent derivative index), and MyHeritage (no relevant results — this collection appears not to be indexed there). Patrick Flynn's 1908 death certificate was found on FamilySearch. A search of Schuylkill County probate records for Thomas Flynn's estate (expected ca. 1870–1890) is in progress and not yet complete; a will or estate administration naming Patrick as a son would meaningfully strengthen this conclusion. Marriage records for Patrick Flynn, the 1870 and 1880 census enumerations, church baptismal records, and Catholic parish registers for the Flynn family have not yet been searched — these record types could independently corroborate or refine this finding. Research is not yet declared exhaustive.
